text: If you were born as Tommy Versetti,
you'd spend 15 years in a cell for a family
that never visited you.
Then they'd send you to paradise
and try to rob you there.
You'd lose everything in one night
and you'd build an empire out of the wreckage,
brick by bloody brick.
But right now, it's the fifties
and you're just a kid on the hard streets
of Liberty City, cold winters, loud neighbors
and men in nice suits who never seem to work
but always have money.
You notice them, you notice everything.
By the time you're a teenager,
you're running small errands for the Forley family.
Deliver a package, watch a door, keep your mouth shut.
You're good at it, too good.
People start calling you reliable
and in Liberty City, reliable
is the most dangerous word there is.
The man who notices you most is Sonny Forley,
sharp suit, big smile, cold eyes.
He treats you like a brother.
At least that's what he says.
Then comes 1971.
Sonny sends you to Harwood to kill one man.
A simple job, but it's a trap.
When you walk in, there isn't one man waiting.
There are 11.
You walk out alone.
By morning, the newspapers have a name for you,
the Harwood Butcher
and the police have you in handcuffs.
The judge gives you 15 years.
Here's the thing about prison.
Everyone talks, everyone cuts a deal.
Everyone gives up a name to get out early.
You don't.
15 years and you never say the name Sonny Forley.
Not once, you keep your head down,
you count the days and you wait.

maybe a little too happy

makes certain people very nervous.
So Sonny has a better idea.
Vice City.
Sunshine, palm trees, neon
and more cocaine than anywhere in America.
The four Lees want a piece of it
and you're the man who's going to get it for them.
Your job is simple.
Fly down, meet the dealers by the product,
send it home.
On the way to the deal,
you meet your new liar, Ken Rosenberg.

and is scared of everything including you.
The deal happens at the docks.
You, Ken and two brothers named Victor and Lance Vance.
Everyone shakes hands.
The briefcase of money goes on the table
and then the shooting starts.
Masked men come out of nowhere.
Victor Vance is killed.
Lance barely escapes.
You and Ken run for your lives.
When the smoke clears, the money is gone.
The drugs are gone
and Sonny's voice comes through the phone, very calm.
He wants his money back.
All of it.
You've been in Vice City for one day
and you already owe the mob a fortune.
So you start where every survivor starts.
You find work.
Ken introduces you to a retired military man
named Colonel Cortez
who knows everybody and trusts nobody.
You do jobs for him.
You make contacts.
You learn the city.
And you meet Lance Vance again.
He's angry, reckless
and he just lost his brother.
You both want the same thing.
The name of the man who set up that deal.
The trail leads to Ricardo Diaz.
Diaz is the biggest drug lord in Vice City.
He's paranoid, loud and dangerous.
And he has no idea that the man he just robbed
is now working for him.
That's right.
You take jobs from Diaz.
You smile.
You run his errands.
And you wait.
Lance can't wait.
He goes after Diaz alone, gets caught
and you have to drag him out of a junkyard full of bullets.
Then it's time.
You and Lance storm Diaz's mansion
room by room,
floor by floor
until there's no one left between you and him.
When it's over Diaz is gone
and the mansion is yours.
Overnight you go from a man with nothing to the man
who owns the most dangerous house in Vice City.

You buy the strip club,
the cab company,
the car showroom,
the film studio,
the print works

Every business makes money.

Cops look away.
Gangs step aside.
People call you mister.

Sonny Forley is watching.
He calls.

Sonny never needed you.
